claims.claim: Calgary councillor Andre Chabot interrupted Matthew Riley, who has Tourette syndrome, during a Friday public hearing on a proposed four-year budget, a 15 per cent property-tax increase and utility-rate hikes, and council recessed for about an hour.
claims.episode_span: Ward 10 Councillor Andre Chabot interrupted a presenter whose tics from Tourette syndrome included profane language
claims.source_title: Calgarian with Tourette syndrome interrupted by councillor during budget public hearing
claims.supporting_quote: A public hearing at Calgary city hall on the proposed four-year budget went into a lengthy recess Friday afternoon, after a councillor interrupted a presenter who repeatedly used profane language due to tics associated with Tourette syndrome.

claims.claim: Mayor Jeromy Farkas apologized, distinguished involuntary disability-related expressions from deliberate disrespect, verified prior notice of the disability, and offered a closed session, which Riley declined before finishing in public.
claims.episode_span: Mayor Jeromy Farkas apologized to Riley for the delay
claims.source_title: Calgarian with Tourette syndrome interrupted by councillor during budget public hearing
claims.supporting_quote: We recognize that involuntary expressions associated with a disability are different from deliberately disrespectful language,” Farkas read from a statement.

claims.claim: Riley told council he would pursue a lawsuit, told Global News he felt hurt and embarrassed and is thinking twice about addressing council again, while Councillor Jennifer Wyness criticized a closed session and Chabot said the public had not been warned.
claims.episode_span: he told council he would pursue a lawsuit
claims.source_title: Calgarian with Tourette syndrome interrupted by councillor during budget public hearing
claims.supporting_quote: He told council during the interruption that he would pursue a lawsuit.

claims.claim: Adriana LaGrange told UCP members in Calgary on Friday that Alberta is reviewing abortion access, that Ottawa requires it to remain available, and that Canada's lack of a law protecting the unborn is a disgrace.
claims.episode_span: Alberta is reviewing access to abortion, Adriana LaGrange
claims.source_title: Alberta government to review access to abortion, health minister says
claims.supporting_quote: “It’s really quite a disgrace that we are the only country in the world that does not have a law in place to protect the unborn,” Ms. LaGrange told the crowd. “But there is a review that is ongoing, and I anticipate getting briefed on that in the very near future, so more to come.”

claims.claim: Sarah Hoffman said the comments attack a woman's right to choose and energize conservative activists, while the Globe and Mail reports Danielle Smith has resisted legislating abortion changes and has not enacted a 2025 resolution on late-term abortion funding.
claims.episode_span: the comments attack a woman's right to choose
claims.source_title: Alberta government to review access to abortion, health minister says
claims.supporting_quote: “It sounds like she found it in attacking a woman’s right to choose. Alberta’s NDP has always and always will stand with women.”

claims.claim: About 2,000 members were in the room and the UCP expects roughly 8,000 in Calgary; Covenant Health does not provide abortions; Ryan Fournier did not immediately respond.
claims.episode_span: About 2,000 members were in the room when LaGrange spoke
claims.source_title: Alberta government to review access to abortion, health minister says
claims.supporting_quote: The UCP expects roughly 8,000 members in Calgary for its annual meeting this weekend. About 2,000 members were in the room when Ms. LaGrange made her remarks.
